messages:
community-bot: Hey @channel — launching the Community Contrib Cookbook v1.0 today! It's a curated set of reproducible, minimal contribs for connectors, quantization recipes, and eval prompts. Repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/community-contrib-cookbook :sparkles:

alexa: huge! where's the quickstart? link?

community-bot: Quickstart is in the README root. TL;DR: docker compose for local dev, a tiny test model, and an eval harness. Snip:
```
git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/community-contrib-cookbook.git
cd community-contrib-cookbook
docker compose up --build
./tools/run_eval.sh --suite minimal
```

joana: Maintainers — please scan MAINTAINERS.md for the new PR labeling schema (priority, compat, test). We're trying a stricter triage flow this cycle. Also heads-up: maintainers sync Wed 10am PT.

matt: I added an "edge-quant" recipe that walks through INT8 quant -> runtime flags -> perf tuning. Local perf (linux, rtx6000): ~2.3x token throughput on 512-length compared to fp16 with tiny quality delta; numbers and plots in /recipes/edge-quant/README.md.

samir: Nice! quick question: will community plugins from the cookbook be eligible for the plugin marketplace? and is there a compatibility matrix for Redwood Dedicated/private deployments?

alexa: Good q. Short-term: we'll tag contribs with `prod-ready` once they pass the CI and have maintainer sign-off. Marketplace eligibility will be a follow-up (ops/product). For Dedicated/Private, check deploy_checklist.md — it lists config knobs and networking guidance.

rajesh: Added a lightweight CI job that runs the minimal eval suite on PRs. It can generate noisy failures at first — please help triage flakiness and file small follow-up fixes.

joana: Also hosting a 1hr office hours session Friday 2pm PT to onboard new maintainers and walk through the cookbook structure :coffee: Register here: https://calendar.redwood.ai/office-hours/cookbook-v1

alexa: Repo tag for release: v1.0.0. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/community-contrib-cookbook/tree/v1.0.0 — thanks to everyone who sprinted on this, especially the maintainers and CI folks :clap:
